planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring after frost danger passes; Sugar Belle is a modern University of Florida release (a cross of Clementine and Minneola tangelo) bred for a combination of cold-hardiness, disease tolerance, and heavy production that has made it an increasingly popular recommendation for Gulf Coast and Southeastern home orchards.

directions: Plant a grafted tree in full sun in well-drained soil and feed with a citrus fertilizer through the growing season; Sugar Belle is a University of Florida-bred mandarin cross prized for its distinctive bell-like shape, deep orange rind, and rich, intensely sweet, honeybell-style flavor, combined with better cold tolerance and canker resistance than many older mandarin varieties. Fruit ripens in winter and holds well on the tree without becoming puffy or losing flavor, giving a longer harvest window than many mandarins. Water deeply but let the soil surface dry between waterings, mulch to protect the root zone, and provide frost protection for young trees during their first couple of winters until they gain size and hardiness.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Citrus Variety Selection
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Citrus for Texas
United States Patent and Trademark Office — Plant Patent PP24,844

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring after frost danger passes; US Early Pride is a USDA-bred navel selection valued for ripening notably earlier than the classic Washington navel, extending the home harvest season into early fall.

directions: Plant a grafted tree in full sun in well-drained soil and feed with a citrus fertilizer through the growing season; US Early Pride is a modern navel orange selection bred for an early ripening window, often ready for harvest well ahead of standard Washington navels, and produces sweet, low-seed, easy-to-peel fruit with the classic navel form. Water deeply but allow the soil surface to dry between waterings, and mulch to protect the shallow root zone from summer heat. Give young trees frost protection through their first winters, and expect a light first crop within a few years of planting a grafted tree, building to full production as the tree matures.
sources: University of California Riverside Citrus Variety Collection
University of Florida IFAS Extension — Citrus Variety Selection

planting.note: Plant after last frost in spring; requires a long frost-free season of 200–240 days to ripen fruit. Hayward is the dominant commercial fuzzy kiwi cultivar worldwide — the standard grocery-store kiwi — and is self-sterile, so a male pollinator vine must be planted nearby for fruit set.

directions: Hayward is the classic commercial fuzzy kiwifruit cultivar behind nearly every kiwi sold in grocery stores, prized for its large size, bright green flesh, and well-balanced sweet-tart flavor. Like all fuzzy kiwi it needs a long, warm growing season and is best suited to zones 7–9 with at least 200 frost-free days; it is dioecious, so a compatible male vine (roughly one male for every 6–8 female vines) must be planted nearby for pollination, since Hayward itself is a female-fruiting cultivar. Train vines on a sturdy T-bar or pergola trellis and prune hard each winter to control the vigorous growth and keep fruiting wood renewed. Harvest in late fall before hard frost once the seeds have turned black, and finish ripening the firm fruit indoors at room temperature.
sources: California Rare Fruit Growers — Kiwifruit Fruit Facts
University of California Cooperative Extension — Kiwifruit Culture
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Fruit and Nut Resources

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March–May. Physical Graffiti is a Florida-origin dragon fruit cultivar highly sought after in hobbyist grafting and collector circles for its exceptionally rich, sugary flavor and vivid magenta flesh, and needs the same sturdy post or trellis support as other dragon fruit.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, sandy to loamy soil against a sturdy post, fence, or trellis for the climbing stems to grip with their aerial roots; Physical Graffiti is a Florida-bred dragon fruit selection that has become a favorite among collectors and backyard grafters for its deep magenta flesh and unusually high sugar content compared with more common commercial varieties. As with other dragon fruit, flowers open only at night and typically need hand pollination with a small brush to reliably set fruit, transferring pollen between blooms of the same or a different self-compatible plant. Treat the plant more like a succulent than a conventional fruit vine — water deeply but infrequently, let the soil dry between waterings, and protect the fleshy stems from any frost, since even brief freezing temperatures can cause serious damage.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Dragon Fruit Production in Florida
California Rare Fruit Growers — Hylocereus and Selenicereus Varieties
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Dragon Fruit for South Texas

planting.note: Plant individual cloves 1-2 inches deep in fall; Silver Rose is a fast-maturing silverskin softneck with a low chilling requirement, tolerating mild Gulf Coast winters better than hardneck types that need sustained cold to divide properly.

directions: Plant individual cloves pointed-end-up, 1-2 inches deep and 4-6 inches apart, in loose, well-drained soil in fall; Silver Rose is a silverskin softneck garlic prized for maturing earlier than many other varieties and for exceptional storage life, often keeping 9 months or longer in a cool, dry pantry when properly cured. Bulbs form tight, papery white to rose-blushed wrappers around a good number of small to medium cloves with a strong, well-rounded flavor that mellows considerably when cooked. Like other silverskins, it tolerates mild winters far better than hardneck types, making it one of the more dependable garlics for zone 8-10 gardens. Harvest when the lower third to half of the leaves have yellowed, cure in a warm, dry, shaded, well-ventilated spot for 3-4 weeks, then trim and store.
sources: Filaree Garlic Farm — Silverskin variety descriptions
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Garlic Variety Selection for Texas
University of California Cooperative Extension — Garlic Production in California
